what: GENERIC LANGUAGE PACK (build L1, 2026-10-21): what engine/tools/language.py uses for any object when no domain pack says otherwise, and under every domain pack (a domain's segmentation and template blocks replace these key by key; its rules come before these). Data only: the tool's code knows no object kind.

segmentation.why: components: separate shells (eyes, teeth, loose pieces) are parts of their own; branches: protrusions of each large shell (limbs, horns, claws, tails, points); shells under min_shell of the surface join what they touch; a shell under split_min_share is not split further. carry_tol: when the model changes, a new face farther than this x the object's size from the old surface counts as new material.

branches.why: all lengths in units of the core radius (the 98th percentile of the inner radius: half the body's thickness in 3-D, the distance to the outline in 2-D). A tip must outlive its merge by tip_persistence; a protrusion is cut where its ring radius grows faster than tan(flare_deg) after at least min_part_length of shaft (engine/tools/language.py branch_segments). function agd: the protrusion function is the average geodesic distance to 32 points spread over the surface (extremities high, the centre low); the geodesic distance from the thickest place (function core) gave the Stanford dragon's claws under 2 mm of persistence because its thickest place sits beside its feet. A protrusion with less area of its own than junction_share x its largest child is a junction piece: it joins what it grows from, and its children grow from that.; a drawing (2-D) keeps function core (function_2d: the average geodesic distance merged the heraldic dragon's hind leg into its body). Any key may be given as key_2d / key_3d for one kind of object only.

facets.why: a facet keeps its faces within facet_deg of its mean normal and covers at least min_facet of the surface and is at least min_facet_width x the object's size wide (a fillet's strip is no facet); the faces between facets go to the two nearest (an edge) or three (a corner: the third within corner_ratio of the second), by walking distance up to edge_reach x the object's size; corners are kept down to min_corner of the surface, other strips down to min_strip; a facet has a planar core: at least facet_core_share of its area within facet_core_deg of its mean normal (a 3 mm fillet's 40 deg band made 4 'facets' at 45 deg on a 12 cm box, prove; an rms-spread limit of 6 deg also refused the brick's frog walls, whose 6 mm flat carries a fillet band)

templates.why: grid step = a readable step near a tenth of the part's size (tubes: its length; discs: the square root of its area); a protrusion at least tube_slender x as long as it is wide at its base gets a tube chart, a part thinner than sheet_flatness of its width two discs (upper, under), a core longer than body_elong x its width a tube along its longest axis, anything else a disc on its mean normal; a facet whose mean normal holds plane_flat of its area (|sum n a| / sum a) is PLANAR: origin at its area centroid, addresses = its frame's x, y by a ray along its normal (h+), as for every part of a 2-D object

findings._: measured findings (build L1, 2026-10-21): what was done, what resulted, where; evidence, not rules

items.what: The protrusion function for a 3-D shape is the average geodesic distance, not the distance from the thickest place
items.result: On the Stanford dragon the thickest place sits beside its feet: distance from it gave no claw over 2 mm of persistence (14 tips over 2 mm on the whole scan); the average geodesic distance to 32 spread points found 22 tips and the horns, spikes, tail fin, feet. On the heraldic 2-D dragon the reverse held: the distance from the thickest place separated all four legs, the average geodesic distance merged one into the body.

items.what: A facet must have a planar core
items.result: Grown within 20 deg of a seed, the middle of a 3 mm fillet on a 12 cm box made 4 facets at 45 deg (at 2 voxels across, marching cubes made the fillet a chamfer). Required: 50 % of a facet's area within 8 deg of its mean normal (an rms-spread limit of 6 deg also refused the brick's frog walls, whose 6 mm flat carries a fillet band). With it: 11 of 11 planted facets, normals within 0.68 deg, outer face areas = flat face + the fillet band within 20 deg (r sin 20 deg per side) within 1.10 %.

items.what: Carry a part's frame on a model change by the rigid fit of its surviving surface
items.result: Re-measured landmarks (area centroids) moved every address of an arris 8.5 mm when a chipped corner took 20 of its 211 mm; carried by the fit (old face centroid to nearest new face centroid, area-weighted) they moved 0.000-0.004 mm (p50). The same carry on a remesh (brick 1.0 -> 0.7 mm voxels): worst part p99 0.27 mm (0.47 mm with re-measured frames).

items.what: Keep a part's template (its kind of address) across model changes
items.result: A part that changed template between builds (disc chart to plane ray address) made every one of its addresses unreadable (no address kind skin); a part whose template has to fall back on the new mesh does the same (cases/dragon3d to res3: foot_L_2, 1,831 addresses). Templates are now kept from the previous build.
items.status: checked; the fall-back case is OPEN

items.what: A part that appears on a changed model must be new material
items.result: Re-segmenting a re-rasterised drawing (1920 -> 1280 px) found a new horn although every new face lay on the old surface (another cut of the same shape); requiring half its area farther than 1 % of the object's size from the old surface removed it, and an erased horn was reported gone with nothing added.

items.what: Grid steps scale with the part
items.result: A fixed 5 cm step cap on a 26 m glTF lantern made 14.6 M grid points (a 1.1 GB page); steps are now 1, 2, 2.5 or 5 x a power of ten near a tenth of the part, never finer than 1/150 of its largest extent: 16,911 grid points, 9 MB.
